A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayerIF and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original expert-allocation and pruning experiments, including benchmark accuracies, ablations and statistical comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds reversed-allocation results in Table 3 and runtime and memory measurements in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 revise IF signs, describe aggregation after sign inversion, and introduce vi = −S(l). However, descriptions of beneficial versus detrimental samples remain inconsistent, preventing a reliable distinction between documentation corrections and changed sample selection. The expert-allocation and pruning mappings otherwise match.

E1.justification: The same five expert-allocation datasets and seven pruning benchmarks remain. The added runtime measurements vary sample counts and model configurations without establishing additional dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds a reversed-allocation comparator in Table 3 and reports a Gauss-Newton-Hessian versus DataInf timing comparison in Section 5. The existing AlphaLoRA/MoLA and Uniform/AlphaPruning/OWL benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include reversed allocation at 70% Mistral sparsity and runtime measurements across three train/validation sample counts and Qwen2.5-3B/32B configurations. Section 4 also changes the stated Mistral version from v0.3 to v0.1, matching existing captions; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct test of the central pruning-direction hypothesis through reversed allocation, plus dataset-size and model-size efficiency analyses in Appendix H and an additional IF-approximation timing comparison. These substantially broaden the analyses beyond the retained sample-selection, smoothing, per-block and TracIn-correlation studies.

E5.justification: The t-tests, significance threshold and reported p-values in v1 Appendix F are retained in v3 Appendix G. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantive new allocation and computational-cost results: Table 3 reports average accuracy of 35.69 versus 34.52 for reversed allocation, while Appendix H adds runtime and memory measurements. Section 5 reports a roughly 160-fold Gauss-Newton/DataInf runtime ratio. Existing benchmark tables and plots retain their values; Section 4.1 changes the aggregate relative-gain summary from 3.54% to 3.52%.

T1.justification: v3 inserts negative signs into the parameter, validation-loss and layer-specific IF definitions and explicitly relates vi to −S(l). These are local mathematical corrections or clarifications. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about data-sensitive layer-quality estimation, its two applications, architecture generality, and the headline 1.61% and 0.90% improvements.

C2.justification: v3 adds noise-filtering and heavy-tail explanations for selecting influential samples, practical cutoff guidance, interpretation of the reversed-allocation experiment, and computational-scaling conclusions. Appendix A's convexity and data-representativeness limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds a numerical allocation walkthrough with beta = 3. Appendix H specifies sample counts, timing configurations, four-GPU hardware and memory consumption for its new measurements. Code-access instructions change from anonymous hosting to named GitHub repositories; their external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained despite reference renumbering. v3 modestly expands positioning relative to Gauss-Newton/EK-FAC approaches and uses the already-cited influence-function literature to motivate smoothing and influential-sample selection.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the introduction, expands Section 5, adds walkthrough and scalability appendices, and corrects wording and cross-references. An acknowledgment and conference footer are added. The overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the reversed-allocation table, two runtime tables and an unnumbered walkthrough table. Figure 2 moves, and Figure 1's caption explicitly identifies its values as illustrative. All four figure images retain identical content; existing displays mainly undergo relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The reversed-allocation control, worked example and measured computational costs improve evidential support and transparency while preserving the original benchmark evidence. The net gain is limited by unresolved influence-sign ambiguity and Appendix H's claims of roughly linear scaling, which its runtime tables do not support.
